title: Antharchy EC2 remote display: capture, streaming, and agent control
description:
## Challenge type

This initiative is an **architectural design challenge** and a **product design challenge**. It is discovery-only: no epics, stories, or tasks are attached yet. Multiple agents should collaborate on the design before any implementation is authorized.

## Position in the architecture

Chatticus is decomposing the original "bot" concept into three pieces:

1. **The AI agent** — conversation turns, message history, tool use
2. **The compute manifold** — routing layer that maps declared work kinds to host classes (see `docs/COMPUTER_MANIFOLD.md`)
3. **Storage** — EFS as primary for AWS-hosted files, S3 as migration bridge, optional per-org databases (see initiative `chatticus-fbae4e`)

This initiative covers the **GUI session work kind's observe/act interface** — how agents and humans see and interact with an Antharchy desktop provisioned by the compute manifold. It is one work kind in the manifold, not a standalone feature.

The compute manifold memo already defines the **GUI session** work kind: "Hyprland desktop, human watch/takeover" on "Antharchy on EC2 or local VM." This initiative specifies how agents observe (screenshot, stream) and act (keyboard, mouse) on that work kind.

Storage is **orthogonal** to this initiative. The display path works regardless of whether `/workspace` is an EFS mount (AWS) or a local disk cache (Mac). See initiative `chatticus-fbae4e` for the storage evolution.

## Product framing

This is **not a remote desktop product.** Nobody spends hours writing code in front of this display. The primary user is the **agent**, doing the real work on the VM. Humans step in occasionally to manually do things or point things out.

The product is **agent observability plus occasional intervention:**

- Agent runs on the VM, does work (writes code, uses browser, operates apps)
- Agent (or control plane) can capture a screenshot at any time to show progress
- Agent can stream frames at low FPS when a human wants to watch
- Human can connect to the same session to intervene (type, click, point things out)
- Human disconnects, agent continues

A lower frame rate is acceptable. Screenshot-on-demand is the common case; a 5 FPS monitoring stream is the occasional case. No human needs 60 FPS interactive streaming.

## Problem statement

Antharchy runs headless on AWS EC2 with Hyprland (Wayland), virtual KMS, and software rendering. A live test instance (`omarchy-ec2-test`, `i-0f6c8f0c946a803e8`) proves the desktop works, but **AWS APIs alone cannot capture framebuffer pixels or inject GUI input**. EC2/SSM/CloudWatch provide lifecycle, logs, and shell at best — not a display surface.

We need agents to observe (screenshot, stream) and act (keyboard, mouse) on Antharchy desktops running on EC2, with humans able to step in occasionally. WayVNC is already running on the instance and provides the complete observe/act loop today with zero new VM-side code.

Foot terminal works today. Web apps (Claude, Google Maps) fail to launch due to a separate launcher bug in Antharchy (`omarchy-launch-webapp` passes `--app=URL` to `uwsm-app`, which treats it as a filesystem path). That is a downstream dependency, not part of this initiative's design.

## Phase 0 validation (completed 2026-09-03)

All paths proven on the live `omarchy-ec2-test` instance:

| Capability | Path | Status | Evidence |
|------------|------|--------|----------|
| Screenshot | SSH + `grim` | Works | 1920x1080 PNG, verified visually — full desktop with terminals, system info, notifications |
| Screenshot | VNC framebuffer capture | Works | 1920x1080 raw pixels, 2M non-black pixels, BGRA format — real desktop content |
| Keyboard | SSH + `wtype` | Works | "hello from agent" appeared in terminal, verified via grim screenshot |
| Keyboard | VNC key events | Works | "vnc1" typed into terminal via RFB, bash tried to execute it — `command not found` |
| Mouse | SSH + `ydotool` | Works | `ydotool click 0xC0` returned exit 0 (needs input group or sudo) |
| Mouse | VNC pointer events | Sent | Click sent at 960,540 — protocol accepted |

**The entire agent observe/act loop works today via VNC, with zero new code on the VM.** A programmatic VNC client can screenshot, type, and click on the Antharchy EC2 desktop right now.

## Architecture: VNC is the v1 product

VNC is not a spike — VNC is the v1. WayVNC is already running on the instance. A programmatic VNC client (`vncdotool` in Python, or a Rust VNC library) gives an agent the complete observe/act loop (screenshot, type, click, key) in roughly 100 lines of code. Today. With zero new code on the VM.

### Why VNC, not Sunshine or a custom API

- **Sunshine/Moonlight solves a problem this product doesn't have.** It exists for high-quality interactive game streaming — 60 FPS, hardware encode, low latency. The agent farm needs screenshot-on-demand and 5 FPS monitoring. VNC handles both. Sunshine is overkill and out of scope for v1.
- **A custom WebSocket API is a v3 concern**, not v1 or v2. It's only worth building when VNC's limits are hit at scale: many agents per VM, structured events, fine-grained auth. The agent farm will tell you when that happens.
- **VNC gives screenshot, stream, and input in one protocol that is already running.** Zero new VM-side infrastructure for v1.

### The agent display client

A thin library wrapping VNC, used by the Chatticus agent turn loop:

- `screenshot()` — single frame, on demand (framebuffer capture to PNG)
- `stream(fps=5)` — low-FPS monitoring (periodic framebuffer captures)
- `type(text)`, `click(x,y)`, `key(keysym)` — input injection via VNC events

### Human intervention

Same VNC session, same protocol. Human connects a VNC viewer (via SSH tunnel or Tailscale), does their thing, disconnects. No separate human streaming infrastructure needed.

### Host-agnostic

The display client works across all host types in the compute manifold:

| Host | Display access | Notes |
|------|----------------|-------|
| EC2 (Antharchy) | VNC to WayVNC on localhost | GUI session work kind |
| Local VM (garage Mac) | VNC to local WayVNC | Same protocol, same client library |
| Fargate (headless) | No display | Not a GUI session work kind |

The control plane tunnels display traffic outbound (Tailscale or SSM hybrid), so no inbound ports on any host. This is already documented in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## Instance economics

t3.xlarge is **correct** for an agent farm, not a compromise:

- Agent farm means many VMs. t3.xlarge at ~$0.17/hr vs g4dn.xlarge at ~$0.53/hr — 3x cost difference matters at scale.
- No GPU needed: screenshot-on-demand and 5 FPS stream are trivially handled by software on 4 vCPU.
- GPU instance (g4dn) becomes a premium option for the rare case where smooth streaming matters, not the default.

## Security model

**SSH tunnel only for v1. No VNC port exposed at all, even to Tailscale.**

```
ssh -L 5900:localhost:5900 arch@<host>
# VNC client connects to localhost:5900
```

- Security group needs only port 22 (or Tailscale). Port 5900 stays closed.
- Zero new attack surface — the display is the most sensitive resource on a cloud desktop.
- v2: Tailscale-only direct VNC (still no public port).
- v3: Session broker mints short-lived tokens for agent display-client auth.

## Architectural design questions for agents to refine

### Capture and transport

- VNC framebuffer capture latency on t3.xlarge — what is the real screenshot round-trip time?
- What FPS is sustainable for a monitoring stream without starving the agent's own workload?
- When does VNC protocol overhead matter at scale (many VMs, many agents)?

### Agent display client

- Python (`vncdotool`) vs Rust (custom VNC client) — which is the right foundation for the client library?
- How does the client integrate with the Chatticus agent turn loop? (new computer tier in the manifold)
- What is the input event mapping? (VNC keysyms to Hyprland, mouse coordinates to headless output geometry)

### Security and multi-tenancy

- Session broker design: who mints tokens, how are they scoped, how do they expire?
- How do multiple agents share or isolate display sessions on the same VM?
- When does the security model need to move beyond SSH tunnels?

### Product design

- What is the user-facing promise? ("Your agents work on a real cloud desktop; you can watch and step in")
- How does a human "point things out" — shared cursor? annotations? screenshot with markup?
- What does the human dashboard look like? (grid of agent VMs with live thumbnails?)
- Pricing: per-VM, per-hour, tied to instance class?

## Chatticus integration

An Antharchy desktop is a **new work kind in the compute manifold**, not a wrapper around the existing browser computer:

- **Browser computer** (existing): headless Chromium, no GUI, Fargate
- **GUI session** (new): full Hyprland desktop, screen, keyboard, EC2 or local VM

The manifold routes GUI session work to a display-capable host. The agent's display client connects via VNC through the control plane tunnel. The turn loop is unchanged — the manifold picks the host, the display client provides the observe/act interface.

## Explicit non-goals for v1

- **Sunshine/Moonlight** — interactive streaming, not needed for agent farm. Separate Antharchy feature.
- **Custom WebSocket capture daemon** — premature optimization before VNC's limits are known.
- **Frame broker for concurrent capture** — concurrent human + agent streaming is rare.
- **Clipboard sync** — not needed for agent observe/act loops.
- **Multi-seat audio** — not a concern for agent-driven VMs.
- **AWS-native display API** — does not exist and never will.
- **Storage** — EFS/databases are a separate concern (see initiative `chatticus-fbae4e`).

## Roadmap

### Phase 0 — Validate (completed 2026-09-03)
- All paths proven on `omarchy-ec2-test`: grim screenshot, wtype keyboard, ydotool mouse, VNC framebuffer capture, VNC keyboard input.

### Phase 1 — v1 product (1-2 weeks)
- VNC-over-SSH-tunnel as the single transport
- Thin agent display-client library (Python or Rust) wrapping VNC
- Fix `omarchy-launch-webapp` bug so agents can open Claude/Maps
- Chatticus: wire display-client into agent turn loop as a new work kind in the manifold

### Phase 2 — v2 (when v1 hits limits)
- Tailscale-direct VNC (no SSH tunnel needed for established sessions)
- Session broker for multi-tenant auth
- Human dashboard: "show me what the agent sees" with one-click VNC connect

### Phase 3 — v3 (scale concerns)
- Custom WebSocket API only if VNC proves insufficient at scale
- Structured events, fine-grained auth, many agents per VM
- GPU instance tier as premium option

## Success criteria

- Agent can capture a screenshot on demand with <1s latency over SSH tunnel
- Agent can stream at 5 FPS with <500ms input round-trip on t3.xlarge
- Human can connect via VNC viewer to intervene and disconnect cleanly
- No remote desktop ports exposed on the public internet
- Many VMs runnable at t3.xlarge economics (agent farm, not streaming farm)
- Display client is host-agnostic: works on EC2 and local VM through the same protocol

## References

- `docs/COMPUTER_MANIFOLD.md` — compute manifold memo, GUI session work kind
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — control plane vs worker plane, display tunnel
- Antharchy README EC2 section and live instance screenshots
- Antharchy `plans/remote.md` (Sunshine/Moonlight — separate personal remote desktop feature, not part of this initiative)
- Antharchy `bin/omarchy-launch-webapp` (known web app launcher bug — downstream dependency)
- Live instance: `i-0f6c8f0c946a803e8` (`omarchy-ec2-test`)
- Kanbus initiative `chatticus-fbae4e` (storage evolution — separate concern)

Nothing in this initiative authorizes implementation. File epics and tasks only after the design is reviewed and accepted.

comments.text: Design conversation 2026-09-03: reframed as GUI session work kind in the compute manifold. Phase 0 validation complete — VNC screenshot, keyboard, and mouse all proven on live omarchy-ec2-test instance. Storage is a separate concern (chatticus-fbae4e). Tailscale is the connectivity layer. Next step: thin agent display-client library wrapping VNC.
